newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND APPOINTS EU INTEGRATION ADVISING COUNCIL.
newsitem.headline: POLAND APPOINTS EU INTEGRATION ADVISING COUNCIL.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Friday appointed a council of businessmen, politicians and experts that would advise the government in prepaprations to accession talks with the European Union.

"The European Integration Council groups economic and legal experts as well as members of the government and non-government political circles," Danuta Hubner, the cabinet minister in charge of European integration, said after the appointments.

The 68-member council gathers chiefs of all parliamentary caucuses, including the opposition, heads of employers' groups, business executives, economists, academics, well-known journalists and cultural experts.
The government would consult the council during preparations for EU membership negotiations, which Poland hopes to start early next year before joining the EU around 2002 or earlier.
The council will also promote benefits that EU membership would bring to Poles and explain obligations connected to the process.
A recent public opinion showed that more than 70 percent of Poles would like to join the EU, but analysts say few of them understand how the EU works.
